hooks.text: Tsutomu Yamaguchi was explaining the Hiroshima blast when the second bomb struck.
How did one man survive atomic bombs in two different cities?
One man survived two atomic bombings just three days apart.

title: How Did One Man Survive Both Atomic Bombs? 🤯
description: Tsutomu Yamaguchi survived the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings in 1945. Japan later officially recognized him as a survivor of both. Archival blast photographs and labeled location cards illustrate the account.

beats.text: Tsutomu Yamaguchi was explaining the Hiroshima blast when the second bomb struck.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Nagasaki atomic cloud, 9 August 1945; the photo depicts the second blast, not Yamaguchi

beats.text: Days earlier, the naval engineer was finishing a business trip in Hiroshima.
beats.visual: Designed Hiroshima, August 1945 location card; no person is depicted

beats.text: At 8:15 a.m., the first atomic bomb detonated three kilometers away.
beats.visual: photograph of the Hiroshima mushroom cloud, 1945
subjects: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

beats.text: Yamaguchi survived the heat and returned home to Nagasaki.
beats.visual: Modern photograph of the Hiroshima Peace Memorial, explicitly labeled as a present-day memorial

beats.text: Bandaged and shaking, he reported for work on August 9.
beats.visual: Designed Nagasaki, August 9 office location card; no person is depicted
subjects: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

beats.text: His supervisor laughed, asking how one bomb could destroy a city.
beats.visual: Return to the Nagasaki office card; no supervisor is depicted

beats.text: Suddenly, the second blast erupted three kilometers from his office.
beats.visual: photograph of the Nagasaki mushroom cloud, 1945
subjects: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

beats.text: He was forced to start his story over.
beats.visual: Reuse of the documented Nagasaki atomic-cloud photograph for the loop

better_than_last: Utilizes a cyclic narrative loop where the concluding action of restarting a story prompts the viewer to rewatch the beginning of that same story.
